title: Arrays: direct access and expensive shifts
summary: Understand why indexing is O(1), why insertion is not, and how two pointers exploit layout.

workedExample.title: Reverse in place
steps: Two pointers start at the ends. They move toward each other; each iteration handles one pair.
The tuple assignment swaps the two values without a temporary variable. It is evaluated before assignment, so it is safe.
After each swap, both pointers have handled their positions, so increment `left` and decrement `right`.
The loop stops when `left >= right`. The middle element of an odd-length array is already in place.
Each element is visited at most once, so the time is O(n). Only the two indices are allocated, so extra space is O(1).

explainPrompt: Why is indexing an array O(1) while inserting at the front is O(n)? Explain using the memory layout.

checkQuestions.prompt: Why is `values[i]` O(1) for an array?
options: The runtime searches for the index from the beginning
The address is computed from the base address and element size
Arrays keep a dictionary of indices
The JIT caches every index access
checkQuestions.explanation: Contiguous elements and fixed size make address arithmetic constant time.
optionExplanations: Arrays do not store an index dictionary.
Caching is not what makes the access constant time.

checkQuestions.prompt: What is the cost of inserting a new element at index 0 of a `List<T>` with n elements?
checkQuestions.explanation: All existing elements must shift right by one position.
optionExplanations: That would be appending when capacity is available, not front-insertion.
A single insertion is not quadratic.

checkQuestions.prompt: What advantage does a prefix-sum array provide?
options: It makes arbitrary range sums O(1) after O(n) preprocessing
It makes insertion at the front O(1)
It reduces memory usage to O(1)
checkQuestions.explanation: Each range sum becomes a difference of two prefix values.
optionExplanations: Prefix sums do not change insertion costs.
The prefix array uses O(n) extra space.

complexityQuestions.prompt: State the time and space complexity of this operation on an array of length n.
complexityQuestions.explanation: Every one of the n existing elements shifts one position to the right. The shifting is done in place, so extra space is constant (the array must have capacity for one more element).

complexityQuestions.prompt: State the time and space complexity of building this prefix-sum array.
complexityQuestions.explanation: The loop runs once over n elements. The returned prefix array has n + 1 elements, which is O(n) extra space.

practice.title: Move zeroes
practice.prompt:
Given an integer array `values`, move every zero to the end while keeping the relative order of the non-zero elements. Do it in place with O(1) extra space.

```csharp
void MoveZeroes(int[] values)
```
hints: Think of a write pointer that marks where the next non-zero value belongs. A read pointer scans the array.
When the read pointer finds a non-zero value, write it at the write index and advance. After the scan, fill the rest with zeroes. Does this preserve relative order?

practice.title: Range sum queries
hints: What information would let you get the sum of `values[0..to]` without adding each element again?
Store cumulative sums in an array of length n + 1. Then `sum(from..to) = prefix[to + 1] - prefix[from]`. Check the indices carefully.
